notes.title: Devlog 19.2: New World
notes.content:
Hello Everyone 😊,

This build focuses on making the game more fun, more interactive, and more immersive. Players who have followed the development of Era will be able to notice differences in almost all facets of the game. From small subtle changes like how the clouds blend in with the sky, to bigger changes like the new trees and new main menu, this build aims to show Era of Survival at its very best.

I will be close by whilst I immediately start on the new build, to spot any problems (if any arises) from this build and will even post another small update with fixes before the next release. I have tested this build myself and involved others and monitored them playing until I see nothing wrong anymore. What I can guarantee you, is that there are no bugs in the game that will stop you from playing until you fall over. 

I really hope this build wows those who have stuck by development all this time. The following changelog will show my dedication and commitment to my project and to those who have supported me and the game so far, as promised and as will continue hence forth. 

[h3]New[/h3]
[list]
[*] New Tree Models
[*] Sleep the night away
[*] Saving and Loading modules have been completely rewritten from scratch. They are now 100% reliable
[*] New models for wooden construction parts
[*] Pick up your Wall Lights with the hammer
[*] Main Menu Background has been reworked and sped up
[*] Background mountains
[*] New Fibre Bush model
[*] Delete World feature in main menu
[*] Wolves howl at night
[/list]

[h3]Removed[/h3]
[list]
[*] Removed puddles, but then butterflies have been kept
[*] Start Tutorial
[*] All Thatch roofs
[*] Simple Knife
[*] Corn Stalks
[*] Ash
[/list]

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed physics when trees fall
[*] Fixed “No Arrows” notification appearing multiple times per second when you run out of arrows and try to pull your bow
[*] Fixed bow pull sound not playing
[*] Fixed rain getting too loud as the storm progresses
[*] Fixed water color to better match the ambience and atmosphere of the specific time of day, also added a sparkle and new ambient sounds
[*] Fixed “Split” menu option when the quantity is 1
[*] Fixed how the Torch is held and how its light affects the surroundings
[*] Fixed UI update on Game Launcher
[*] Fixed notification text overlapping its background
[*] Fixed stairs place holder
[*] Fixed all hammer related bugs. If its yours, then you can pick it up now
[*] Fixed Fireplace not producing cooked food but deducting raw food
[*] Fixed active tool breaking on reload
[*] Fixed animals walking in the air over what looks like an invisible bump
[*] Fixed fish fly away through the air when your rod breaks whilst pulling the fish in
[*] Fixed running under water, animals running under water and underneath, also fixed objects spawning in water
[*] Fixed moon rising through the terrain
[*] Fixed misaligned GUI at death screen as well as listing of destroyed beds
[*] Fixed lights and signs spawning deep inside walls
[*] Fixed farm base shows 100% progress but nothing can be picked up or seen, even if you saw the less mature plant earlier
[*] Fixed Crafting Station indicator stays on even if you left the vicinity of the Crafting Station
[/list]

[h3]Performance Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Optimized all Rock models
[*] Various code in game got optimized by implementing coding best practices and strategies that can deliver the same result but much faster
[*] Fixed FPS drops around Wooden Foundations
[*] Improved FPS around wall lights and improved light colors and brightness
[*] Fixed FPS drops during rain
[/list]

[h3]Additional Adjustments[/h3]
[list]
[*] Adjusted the cost of beds
[*] Adjusted forest sounds
[*] Adjusted many game sounds to improve the general harmony at any point in time in the game
[*] Adjusted game atmosphere, clouds, fog, and visual effects to better match the games personality
[*] Various GUI improvements to make menus more interactive and easier to read
[*] Firewood lasts twice as long
[*] More emphasis is now placed on your world within the GUI
[*] New worlds start time is now at 7 AM, instead of 11 AM
[*] Added forward facing arrows to Crafting Station and Multitasking Station
[*] Craft Queue length is now 9 from 10
[*] Added more game tips to show on the loading screen
[*] You will now get one seed when eating veggies, not 2
[*] Lettuce has been made more prominent
[/list]

I hope you are excited to go and experience these changes, yes things are radically different since the last build! I myself play, and to confess, some of the things on the list were things I wished were there. If you did too, today is your lucky day! If you don’t own a copy yet, get one and join in on the adventure and witness firsthand as Era grows and expands.

Cheers 😊 
And on to implementing the next adventure!

notes.title: Devlog 19.1: Misty-Blue Afternoons
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

I am happy to bring you Devlog 19.1, a very special build for me. This is a build that I have carefully combed through piece by piece over the last few months. My goal was to rewrite code to make things simpler and faster. I will admit that my strong points aren't exactly 3D modeling and animation, so don't expect too many changes in those departments here. Instead, I focused on bug fixes and improving what would make the experience more chilling and fun immediately. I am happy to say that most of these fixed bugs are game breakers - so let's dig into a world where we never have to deal with all these problems again :)

[h3]Loading/Saving Bugs:[/h3]
* Fixed a bug where all game timers would be 10 times slower after loading your game. Evident with a fire burning and cooking and day/night cycle speeds. 
* Fixed a bug where if you saved your game while it was raining, it would never stop raining when you loaded your game again
* Fixed a bug that happened every time you closed your inventory, which scrambled your save file after opening the inventory about 40 times. This corrupted your entire save file 

[h3]Visual changes:[/h3]
* Adjustments to the atmosphere in the game with procedural Fog during normal weather
* Adjustments to the atmosphere in the game with procedural Fog and lighting effects during rainy weather
* Many textures and materials have been reworked and refined. Most evident in render speed and disk space usage
* More fauna and flora around the world to make the world feel more like a place you can call home, a place that provides to all those whose only willing to take it

[h3]Frame rate related bug fixes:
[/h3]* Fixed massive frame drops when placing wooden foundations as well as weird terrain flicker when walking through a house that was carved into a slope or mountain ridge when originally built. I have removed the part where you carve out the mountain too when placing your foundation.
* Fixed frame drops when many items were present around the player
* Fixed further frame drops around water bodies, also changed the look and feel of the dams. Also fixed footstep sounds at dams

[h3]Gameplay fixes:
[/h3]* Fixed a bug where you pick something up (like a mushroom), it disappears off the ground, but your backpack was full, so the item is gone.
* Fixed a bug that was throttling speed on animal response and reaction times. Wolves and bears are now as aggressive as intended. 

[h3]Other changes/bug Fixes:[/h3]
* Entire project has been updated to the newest version of Unity. All legacy code from when the game was initially worked on in Unity 5.6.4 has been updated to Unity 2021.
* As with Unity 2021, the initial "Display Screen Resolution Dialog" that comes with Unity has been removed. Screen resolution can now be set on the Graphics page in the Settings Menu.
* Reduced the cost of most construction items.
* Decrease health of Chicken, they are now easier to kill. Don't worry if you killed many, they will soon respawn again in their numbers.
* Improved loading world speed and removed the choppiness (Not responding) 
* Multiplayer mode is getting a similar comb through, so is currently placed in Experimental mode. I recommend LAN sessions and even same country WAN sessions, but high latency sessions would cripple the experience quickly.
* Improvements with object collisions (There was a specific type of rock that was spawned 150 times over the map whose collider was wrong, this bug fix also fixed this)
* Fixed bug with opening and closing doors eventually stops working. How fantastic? My door wouldn't open that one time I really didn't need it to let me down.. Gone Satan!
* Fixed a bug where a silent error would occur in the server which would even shut it down, without ever notifying the player, who would still be running around with a weapon that lasts forever.. 

I really hope players enjoy this build of Era of Survival. I am glad to offer you a more seamless and immersive - yet unique in its own way - experience. I am thankful to the small community out there that continue to send me supporting and motivating messages. Thank you for sticking to Era of Survival, see you in-game!

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 19: The Craftsman
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

This build focuses on improving the player's ability to craft things in the game. Using new placeable items like the Crafting Station and Multi-Tasking Station, players can now craft much faster and even two things at once! I also spent a considerable amount of time debugging various systems in the game, just to make things smoother. If you haven't yet, pick up your copy of Era of Survival and see what it's all about, or add Era of Survival to your wishlist and stay in the loop!

And now.. The expansion of crafting in Era of Survival.

[h3]Crafting Station - Tier 1[/h3] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/347a1dbdf2a8d1796cfc16b9d69dd347c85d320a.png[/img]
A crafting station lets players in close proximity to it, craft items faster. The station also opens up a 'Crafting Station Tier 1' Crafting section with items you can exclusively craft only when you're close to the crafting station. The tier 1 station will be used to craft advanced tools as well as the Multi-Tasking station

[h3]Multi-Tasking Station[/h3] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/087f85aed7700d465ef5906d48f16cc301c09bcc.png[/img]
This station gives the player the ability to craft two things at the same time. If you have three things in your craft queue, with number one currently crafting, if you were close to a Multi-Tasking station, number two in the queue would also start crafting. If you were close to a crafting station, both slots would craft faster too.

[h3]Stone Arrows[/h3]
Similar to the wooden arrow, but does more damage on impact. They do require stone to make but can be worth it in a tight corner

[h3]UI Cosmetics[/h3]
I adjusted the GUI in the main menu a bit for uniformity. Page widths and heights now match, the scroll box showing your worlds scrolls far enough to show all your worlds, even if there are 37 of them. They might sound like simplistic fixes, but they can look pretty stupid if just left as is

[h3]New foliage[/h3]
Players will see new flowers and weeds between the grass. Together with modifications to rocks and how they are placed, the terrain almost looks brand new. I also worked on sounds in the forests, as well as the ecosystem in the forest. Just go into the forest, it's not so scary :)

[h3]Bug: Placement with fire[/h3]
The fire's comfort and heat range that affects the player seems to have interfered when you wanted to place other things around it. I have separated the placement system from this range system (which is also used by the Multi-Tasking Station and Crafting Station) so they no longer interfere with one another, meaning you can place items close to the fire, but obviously not on top or in any way intersecting. This would also have been the cause for why you couldn't place walls when you have placed a fire.

[h3]New Sounds[/h3]
I have replaced the Main Menu sound with a better nature sound and replaced the doomsday sound when you load your world with something more welcoming.

The list is not long, but this build lays the foundation to start expanding. It is now much easier to add new items and objects to the game, I can now focus more on the item I'm adding, than focusing on how it will be implemented.. Devlog 19 will have a 19.1, most likely a 19.2 and maybe a 19.3. In Devlog 20 I want to add the first native, who would be recruitable to do jobs for the player, like collect wood, water or tend to farm bases, go fishing or defend you. 

I want to say thank you to those who keep sending their best wishes, nice thoughts, and positive comments. There is a moment of silence in appreciation whenever I come across any of the above. Thank you for your support and motivation, just look at how far it took Era! The community's involvement and feedback is key and is clear for all to see

There's still lots to do, and time is limited! So with that said, off I go.

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 18: Kill or be killed
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

Today I bring you a new threat, new sounds, new foods, and some new UI touches. This build aims to make the grasslands a harsher place to live in. Here's what's new:

[h3]Improvements to In-Game Chat[/h3]
I changed how chats are seen in-game but most of the work was in the background. Players benefit from having the chats take up less space and are easier to read than in previous builds.

[h3]Load from last checkpoint[/h3]
When you die, you will now see a new button called 'Load from last Checkpoint' which you can use to reload your game from the last save, be it via autosave or manual. 

[h3]No running whilst aiming[/h3]
When you pull your wooden bow, as soon as you start to aim, you will no longer be able to run until you stop aiming. You may walk around still, but your target won't start walking instead of running too..

[h3]UI - Crafting[/h3]
I changed how the resource requirement per craft item is shown in the Crafting menu. Instead of reading '100 wood, 100 stone', you will now see the correct icon for the resource with the amount needed.

[h3]Creative Mode and Instacraft[/h3]
You can now turn on Creative Mode and Instacraft when starting a new world in the main menu via the toggle under 'World Name'

[h3]New Brown Bear[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/1588fa6557c3658355ab891a6ca37bd1ac8458b8.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/0b2b7f0b2d0c0da871190dbb4c0f42382263eb06.png[/img]
The grasslands have new residents and they are not friendly to others. These bears will not hesitate to storm and kill you. They are fast and strong and will attack you non-stop until you either run away or win the fight. The upside is that, because they are big animals, they can provide quite a lot of meat that can be cooked and eaten. It would be best to avoid them or take them on from a distance.

[h3]Thatch Roof Single[/h3]
This is the only roof part I'm freezing rotation on because it doesn't look good when rotated and then placed at 30 degrees. It looks best when rotation is the same as its corresponding floor.

[h3]Where is the chickens?[/h3]
It seems a bug from Devlog 17.3 caused the chickens to not spawn at all. They are back, but there will only be 10 of them on the map.

[h3]New Sound Settings Tab[/h3]
Here you can set the Master Volume for the entire game using the slider.

[h3]New Sounds[/h3]
Fence Gate open and close sounds
Cup Splash sound when fetching water from dams and ponds

Unfortunately, the survival guide will have to come a little later. To get it all together, I must document most items in-game into a single guide which will be available via the settings menu in-game, detailing every single thing in the game. Luckily so far there are only 96 different items and over 30 different elements identified to add to the survival guide. Whilst I might not include all of them, I'll certainly try and be as clear as possible. 

I want to say thank you to those who follow me and Era of Survival. The difference between what I launched with versus what I'm posting today is vast and undeniably clear. It is the input from the community that makes this difference possible. Thank you very much for the support, motivation, advice, and encouragement. Together we will build and grow Era until it is the jewel it can be and a game we will cherish for years to come :)

Cheers!
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 17.3 Minor fixes
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

This is a small build that fixes minor UI, sound, and gameplay bugs. They are mainly to improve gameplay. 

[h3]Fixed an issue where fire would start on spawn[/h3]
Some players reported that when placing a fire, the flames would turn on when placed, even if there's no wood in it. Extinguishing the fire, then turning it on again solved it. This has been fixed and behaves as expected.

[h3]Fixed an issue with draggy sound, caused by aSync[/h3]
To bring down RAM requirements for the game, music playing in-game streamed from the hard drive when needed, and no longer via RAM. This is okay when you have an SSD or a not-so-busy traditional hard drive, but some players experienced what I didn't want, stretchy sound.. Loading music from RAM brings RAM usage up again, so I managed to load only sounds that will be needed soon, versus loading all music when you load your world up.

[h3]More cloth will now spawn around the map[/h3]
When a new world is created, cloth bushes are spawned in groves, where they are predominantly, just like all the wolves. You will now find more random spawning cloth around the map as well with the current quantity within groves preserved. Many players seem to avoid groves (the group of trees that looks like a forest), then I receive complaints that there's no cloth, no food, no animals, barely any water on the map - when all of this can be found in the grove.. 

[h3]Wolves[/h3]
I decided against adding more wolves because players can already add more wolves through the server settings page. This defaults to 20 random lone wolves spawned across the 2 square kilometer map, with between 6 and 8 living in a pack in each grove. So, finding wolves in wide-open spaces is rare, they live in packs inside the grove predominantly. If one chased you until outside the grove and gave up, he'll even walk back to join his pack again.

Guys, I must level with you, Today I'm actually someone who's on his 4th consecutive day of sick leave. I haven't been a stranger to sick leave in the last couple of months either, I'm actually not all that healthy. I'm at my 3rd job since the first lockdown in March last year (which was like a month after Eras launch and did its part to slow down development), these days it seems there are more days where the power would be off at night than on, thanks to our broken national electricity company (not to mention the 2 expensive RAM sticks I've lost myself due to power surges when the lights come back on). I have a wife and toddler to provide for as well - it seems crises and compounded stress is around every corner, which is making bankrolling a multiplayer survival game all the more difficult. Whilst I have lots of ideas and plans for Era, sometimes you're blocked from actually getting things implemented for reasons that are beyond your control. I can go on and on about all the challenges indies face when trying to make games. 

I mention this so you can expect slow development when you decide to buy Era of Survival. There is one person filling all the roles of game development. It takes a lot of time and resources to get anything implemented in this game, and as is obvious, the scope of work is very big. Just ask the guy from Subsistence (a similar game that is almost 5 years old and also solo developed, don't know if that includes making the assets too)

I'm going to continue working on Devlog 18 now, I hope to finalize a new enemy, a survival guide, bring new sounds, as well as fix more bugs. Phase 2 of development will begin by Devlog 20, where you will be able to establish your own colony, with your own AI followers that you can give jobs to (like chop wood, fetch water, defend the base - to name a few). Until then, thank you for your interest in Era :)

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 17.1: Bug fixes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/dd3280ace7bdee41836ad2738035bb16b5ad60ac.png[/img]

Hello Everyone,

This build mainly focuses on fixing bugs found across various gameplay elements (Construction, placement, game -> server optimizations to name a few). This build doesn't bring new big features, instead it's all about smoothing gameplay. 

Have a look at everything that's changed:
[list]
[*] I decided to retire the Decorative logs and Turnips, the logs contribute to fluctuating frame rates and the turnips are losing their place in the game's natural ecosystem with every new build we publish. Unfortunately, the turnips have become too foreign to the rest of the game objects.
[*] Resized in-game chat section on the server settings page
[*] Saving inventory optimized to fix rare occasions where the latest inventory items are not saved when force-quitting
[*] Adjusted rain intervals and changed the rain color
[*] When you cast your hook into the water, the splash didn't always splash
[*] Fixed bug where all other player names were 'JMG' and their armor would be invisible
[*] Fixed a bug where whilst holding a bow and using the inventory, you would hear the bow cancel sound play
[*] When using any actions in the inventory, the items will now first be removed before the result is received (When you Clean a fish, instead of getting the fish fillets and then giving the fish, now you will give the fish and then get the fish fillets)
[*] Fixed a bug where on rare occasions the Hammer tool could be used to pick up anyone's construction parts, where you should only be able to use it to pick up your own construction parts
[*] There is now an 800ms limit before you can close your backpack from the time you opened it. This buffer exists to ensure the server and game finished syncing. 
[*] New Cheat: Teleport feature. This is currently restricted to server moderators who can find the correct info within the game server (through the Dev view hidden page). Soon this will be released so that you can teleport to others (or setpoints) that can be teleported to in creative mode or through a flag in the server settings.
[*] Wall Lights and Fires are now brighter
[*] "Door locked!" Notify when you try and open a door of which you don't have the key
[*] Fixed a bug where loading different worlds could leave the Creative mode and Instacraft toggles on the server out of sync
[*] The settings page is currently undergoing work so that we can introduce key-mapping. But for this build, we have disabled pages for input, sounds, graphics, and the survival guide as they are not ready.
[*] We tweaked how fish will battle when you try and fish them. You will have to subdue them a little more to reel them in
[*] Adjusted snapping construction parts, they should not interfere so easily with one another now
[*] Various minor system adjustments and internal simplifications bring a 10 - 20fps increase, depending on the system. This is to allow lower-end computers to enjoy the game.
[/list]

Sadly there wasn't enough time to bring a new feature as well, but I felt that these fixes will make an immediate difference when you play. So enjoy them whilst I work on the next best idea. In the mean time, thank you for following Era, thank you for your time and thank you for the support :)

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 17: Bigger fish to fry!
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

This build brings new features, new craftable items, new animals, new tools, new sounds, new animations, and a wide range of big and small bug fixes. This build introduces a new triangular wooden foundation, dams filled with fish, and a fishing rod to fight them out of the water. These changes bring new ways you can play and explore Era. 


[h3]Updated Start Menu[/h3]
To show what's possible with Era of Survival's build system, we decided to change the start menu screen. This structure took about 20 minutes to put together with InstaCraft and Creative mode enabled. 

[h3]New Animals[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/fab7df65528098628a13ef3be6afaae8f213bb07.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/331ff0aec53aeff9359956cc5fc9b10babf75243.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/aea4cbeb7942a118b9ab0d3f4062b228d36f6d46.png[/img]
We introduce 3 new fish, the Perch, the Pike, and the Trout. They can be found swimming together in dams minding their own business. If you cast your rod into the water, they might take the bait, or might pass on it. They may change their mind, patience is key in fishing. Every dam will have a different amount of fish in it, ranging from 30 to 50 fish. Dams are depletable but will respawn fish after a few days. 

[h3]Fishing and the fishing rod[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/53ec12b1d87474452d37d88e11f29993502b4d49.png[/img]
With a new fishing rod in hand, you can now go fishing! Go up to one of the four dams on the map, stand outside on the terrain, use the red dot in the middle of your screen to aim where you'd like to cast, look up or down depending on how far you'd like to cast and then cast. Wait until you see your line move, indicating a fish took the bait and then strike. Use a combination of pulling and reeling to fight the fish out of the water. The fish are temperamental and will use all their strength to avoid getting pulled out of water. There are 3 different species of fish, whose fillets, once cooked, influences hunger and thirst differently. Just don't throw in obviously shallow waters near the shore, unless you see a fish there, don't cast there.. 

[h3]Triangular wooden foundations[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/4d5be6e69e212eaa9ff6f029f2b42d5c3f932609.png[/img]
A real delay causer.. Some extra TLC was needed to get the last squeaks out of this one. They said I would never use anything I learned in school in real life.. And out of nowhere, bam! Trigonometry. This foundation opens a world of new designs for your structures. You can now build pentagonal structures attached to your squared structures or build triangular posts against your home. Place one down and you will easily see how to build onwards from there. 

[h3]Bug Fixes:[/h3]

Error when the server starts. This relates to an issue involving upper armor and lower armor interfering with the hunger and thirst system. The error means that there's an error processing a number trying to be hunger/thirst when it's supposed to be a leather vest.. This fix solves issues with all these systems together. They will all sync properly now.

Split/Discard option for all. These options are now defaulted options for everything in the backpack and can be found aligned bottom right in the backpack. 

Improve the look of water. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/8f429ba560f70dc0c910cc20cc046e3d3b1e878a.png[/img]
In one of our first builds, when we introduced dams the first time, we introduced a sleek looking water body as our dam, but many players experienced frame drops and even temp pauses when moving around the water, so we decided to rather lower the quality on the body seeing that we couldn't find what was causing these performance issues.. Whilst implementing the fishing system, I finally found what the cause was (wayyy by accident) and managed to fix it. Now we have nice looking water, without strange performance drops.

Placement issue. When you placed doorways or fences and equipping a wall or construction part to snap like a wall, you would see the white placeholder flicker on and off constantly. This will now just be switched off or on as it should. I also found issues with other construction parts that under certain circumstances when placing would not place (denied) or the white placeholder would just not be shown, preventing you from placing your wall. I reviewed all of their compatibilities with one another and fixed any issues I could find. Let me know if you find anything buggy or unstable in the build system :)

Raining through the roof. A personal pest.. Whilst the roof parts look simple in design, they actually consist of quite a few parts, and finding out where all these intermittent and unpredictable roof leaks come from, was frustrating, to say the least.. It turns out this was related to the collision quality of the raindrops, after some tweaking, all the leaks disappeared! 

[h3]Carry over:[/h3]
We will have to carry over key mapping again. Unfortunately, we need to do more research to find a different approach, what we have currently does not pass internal tests and is unstable.. We had to revert all key mapping efforts to what players have come to know.

It was fun testing these features, I find being able to now build in different directions changes the picture when it comes to designing a home. The fishing system was also fun, like everything Era, no fish battle is the same. I hope players enjoy them as much as I did. We thank every person that takes the time to leave us an encouraging comment, send us a happy email or send us ideas and new insights, any support on any level is heavily valued. Whether financial, technical, creative or even just a nice comment, it has big impact, I say thank you to you for being part of our community!

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 16: Hunters arise!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36714269/1a819ff1c5d52c92a7cddd7015e5cfc70cb5e5cf.png[/img]

Hello Everyone,

In this build, we wanted to expand construction, hunting, and self-defense. We also introduce bigger stones to mine from, the rest of your armor suit, and a hammer! There's also some adjustments we've made, and as our main priority - bash bugs. 

Unfortunately, custom key mapping could not make it into the final build and will have to roll over to our next build. This feature needs extensive testing to make sure it doesn't end up breaking game flow completely because of small errors.

There's a few topics to cover here, so pull up a chair and your cup of coffee! I certainly did.

[h3]The homemade Bow[/h3]
We're excited to finally get our players hands-on with our bow. This is how it works. To shoot an arrow, craft a bow and a few wooden arrows. Then put your bow in one of the slots in your belt and equip it. Hold Right Click on your mouse to load the bow. Once ready, press left click to shoot whilst holding right-click still. If you keep holding Right-click in, your avatar will reload again. To stop, just stop holding down right-click. 
To start off with, we introduce wooden arrows, which don't kill on contact. 5 arrows will bag you a wolf. Aim above the target, aim higher if the target is further away. Use the red dot in the middle of the screen for guidance. We plan to add other arrows as well, like arrows that explode on contact or combusts on contact.

[h3]New Hammer[/h3]
The purpose of the hammer is to repair your construction parts, like walls, windows, foundations, doors, roofs or stairs. You can also use the hammer to pick up these parts and re-place them somewhere else. There's a few things to know here though. When repairing your parts, the hammer will charge 80% of the needed resources to fix a chunk of wall. Consider that a wall costs 125 wood. To repair it from 1 health back to 100 health, it will end up costing 100 wood. So its 20% cheaper to repair items in stead of building new ones. You must have the supplies available in your backpack. 
You can only pick up an item that [u]you[/u] built. Whether in a previous session or current, if you didn't build it, you can't repair it or pick it up..

[h3]New Stone Door item[/h3]
Works the same as the more familiar wooden door. It is stronger and costs stone to make. 

[h3]New Clothing items[/h3]
Player armor is handled through the players clothing system. In the previous build we introduced the leather vest as well as the leather pants. We now complete the set with cover for your head and a pair of boots. These clothing items do take a toll temperature wise, each item will make your avatar warmer, making you thirsty quicker in the process.
The boots will make you walk and run faster, but that will also make you thirsty quicker.

[h3]Too strong roof parts[/h3]
This might sound unnessesary, seeing that you can now just pick it up, but we looked if it's still needed to adjust the strength of roof parts, and found that compared to other construction parts and their costs, the roofs are a little too strong. They have been dialed back health-wise.

[h3]Health and hunger reset on login[/h3]
In previous builds, when you got hungry or thirsty, you could simply fill both bars by reconnecting to the server or saving and loading your offline world. This has been fixed. I'm sure this will re-instill the quest for survival.

[h3]Issue with signs[/h3]
We made a change to a system that controlled how much resources must be given to the player when you use tools. This swopped a sign from being a breakable item, to a harvestable item giving signs on impact. This has been fixed. You can now again break your signs

[h3]Changes to Construction[/h3]
Placing any building parts or placeables will now make your player a little thirsty and hungry. You will also find arrows that shows you in which direction the part is facing. For doorways, to have the lock inside the house, make sure the doorway's arrow is facing forward, and not at the player.

[h3]Knife[/h3]
We noticed that the knife stopped working completely. We reinstalled the knife and it seems to respond properly now.

[h3]Unit System toggle[/h3]
The toggle under settings that you use to change the unit system in game (from Celcius to Fahrenheit) disconnected and did nothing when you changed it. This is fixed.

We keep striving to improve and expand Era of Survival in many different facets of the survival genre. Sometimes we face bugs that takes hours of research to fully understand and fix, sometimes one fix can fix the bug, and ends up breaking something else down the line. 
The scope of the game is still big, but we divide it into bite-sized chunks and prioritize to have the most stable result possible when we ship a build, whilst adding something new, and something game-changing. We do this for our supporters, always hoping to surprise you guys with something new.

We hope that players welcome the new changes and features, certainly, the bug fixes will be appreciated :)

Cheers for now!
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 15: New Armor, new SFX, new features and more
notes.content:

At the same time, we wanted to get the foundation ready for avatar clothing, and while we are at it, add a few new effects while we remove stuff that wasn't working out for our players. The armor bar in your belt shows average health between all your armor. When you open your inventory, you can see the new Clothing bar on the left hand side of your backpack. To wear any piece of clothing, click on it in your backpack and click the "Wear" option at the bottom. Armor will provide damage protection against any attack, torso and leg protection will absorb as well as take damage differently and soon enough, across different grades of clothing with different strengths.
[h3]Split items in your inventory[/h3]
We found it an urgent need to add the ability for players to split any stackable items in their inventory into any amount they wished. When you click on a stackable item in your backpack, a new option "Split" will be available at the bottom. Simply click "Split", type in how much and click the "split" button. That's it!
[h3]Notable tweaks[/h3]
[list][*]We added some butterflies that can be found flying around small ponds, in the large groves.[/*][*]You will also notice that we made changes to a few of the sounds that you've come to expect. We have replaced this with a nice special effect rather[/*][*]GUI background for the belt and the crafting queue have been updated[/*][*]Tool animations have been improved. They are not new though, but a lot more easy on the eyes.[/*][/list]
 

We hope that our players see the differences these changes make to gameplay. We say thank you to those who support Era of Survivals growth and development. Every comment, every suggestion, every bug report - it is the community's moral support, their patience and understanding and willingness to help us push the boundaries, it is for this reason why our community is the beating heart of any project. Thank you truely, guys. 

 

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Small Update: Save your World
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

Just a small update to bring about some big change in gameplay. This build enables a move away from "playing offline" to "Single Player", we also fixed an issue with the player's belt and fixed a placement bug.

[h3]Load and save[/h3]
Players can now create a new world through the Single Player option in the main menu. You name your world. Your world will autosave every 10 minutes, or you can save in the in-game settings menu or when going to the main menu. Players can create as many worlds as they like.

[h3]Issue with belt[/h3]
There was an issue where the tools and weapons you have in your belt (the 5 slot strip at the bottom of the screen) would disappear when you exit and enter the game. This has been fixed. 

[h3]Placement bug[/h3]
A bug was present whereupon equipping a placeable item like a storage box, fireplace, or even a wall, initially placement would be denied by highlighting the object in red. Swopping between slots seems to have been a quick fix. This has been rectified. Object placement collision will now respond appropriately.

[h3]Forever Pitch dark bug[/h3]
We picked up a while ago that a handful of players were met with a completely pitch black landscape when starting a game playing offline. As if time was not moving and it was constant night. We managed to replicate the issue and it seemed to have been from older graphics hardware and their compatible shader model, however as German user Chaoshexe communicated his experience to us, it became clear that this was related to the fact that Windows would have different regional settings set on his computer. 
After investigation, we found that this graphical issue is because of his decimal separator, being a comma. In some countries, a comma is used as a decimal separator. In other countries, a dot is used. What happened is that time would be synced as a decimal, and between the game and the server there was confusion over the comma. So we have now learned and fixed - Thank you for your input, Chaoshexe!


We are currently knee-deep with Devlog 15, but we felt that the ability to load and save a world would give players the opportunity to turn their houses into the palaces they want. The bugs addressed also weighed heavily on the urgency. We want our players to have a stable gameplay experience, not a frustrating one where constant hiccups ruin the immersion. 

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 14: The new Dawn
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

In this build we focused on bringing new features and enhancements to Era, we also addressed a few bugs and made changes which will dramatically improve the pace during gameplay. Tools and weapons have been strengthened and are more durable. We also changed the wolf and worked on his AI to make him a better enemy. Further we made effort to make this build our most stable yet.

Admittedly, since Devlog 13, we have been through a rollercoaster in South Africa trying to dodge a humanitarian disaster due to covid, whilst same time trying to keep people from losing their jobs, houses and livelihoods. This balancing act by our government had - properly - shaken even the most remote resident of our country and had a devastating impact on the ground. Some describe our country's response as the harshest in the world, draconian even. I mention this because I feel that players need to understand the situation my team found ourselves in after releasing Era in early access. 

As a small team, the buck stops with us to finance and develop Era of Survival, something greatly jeopardized by macro influence, something we could have never seen coming mid Feb when we launched. In general it is known that Indie games do not generate 'big bucks' and normally the cost of running and developing, far exceeds income. Please keep this in mind when you judge Era. If you don't know what the term 'loadshedding' means, then you won't really understand the time gap between Devlog 13 and Devlog 14. Just google 'South Africa', and if your not from here, be very very glad!

Now that we got all that moaning and groaning out of the way, here is the juicy stuff :)

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Rain occurs less frequent, is less harsh and will not rain the same amount every time. 
Sometimes it will storm, other times you may only encounter a light shower
[*] Storage Box Drag and Drop combination of items fixed
[*] You can now break wall lights
[*] Trees will now fall at a decent linear and angular speed
[*] Chickens will now crow only in the mornings, while crickets will only be heard at night
[*] Object placement and collision upon placement has been fixed
[*] Temperature influence from camp fire has been increased, however you cannot put other objects too close to the fire
[/list]

[h3]New[/h3]
[list]
[*] Signs
Players can now peg a sign outside with a custom message, or attach it to a wall, like a wall light
[*] Roof Tops
This build introduces 3 new construction parts, a thatch roof corner, a thatch roof extension and a single thatch slab roof. You must snap them to the white placeholders generated by the foundation
[*] New Stairs
We added railing to the stairs to prevent players from accidentally falling off when they quickly run up the stairs
[*] Door Auto-Close feature
When on, all doors will close 3 seconds after being opened automatically. By default this is disabled. This setting can be found on the server. 
[*] New Wolf
We changed the skin of our wolf, apart from his behavior he looks completely different
[/list]

[h3]Enhancements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Weather, starvation and thirst stabilization
Weather, starvation and thirst will take much longer to kill the player. Rain is barely ever dangerous, but in very low temperatures, you can still freeze to death.
[*] Tools and weapons have been enhanced
Resources gathered from tools have almost been doubled, trees will deplete much sooner and players will be able to build houses much earlier in the game.
[*] Sky, lighting and atmosphere adjustments
This improves the overall look of the game whilst it transitions through its day/night cycle.
[*] Rain - clouds will grow darker and thicker
[/list]

During these stressful times, it is that one message of encouragement that can sometimes keep a developer sane. My team and I want to express our gratitude to the few that has stayed in contact and kept supporting our project. We are firm on our commitment to you, to keep moving forward and to bring our shared dream to the fore for us all to enjoy. 

Until next time,

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 13: Bug bashing
notes.content:
Hi Everyone, 

For this build we decided to take a moment and start cleaning up bugs. Whilst this build mainly focuses on bugs, we also replaced the water well with something new, fixed character animations, polished the wolf some more and made a few convenience changes here and there. We also turned down the severity of heavy rains. We spent additional time testing on this build and would like to hear our players opinion on this build :) Without further delay, here we go!

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Player dies over and over on the respawn screen
This bug was due to the new Auto Heal feature that was introduced in Devlog 12. What happened was the server would Auto Heal dead players in its registry. If your avatars health was below zero and you died from cold, Auto Heal will increase your health to 1, the cold will decrease it by 1. Every time your health reaches or reaches below 0, the server spawns your dead body and backpack. As a result a pile of dead bodies and backpacks would be scattered around, all backpack's supplies would look the same and would look like your current backpack too, because they all share the same reference in the server's registry. 
[*] Hide GUI on death and settings screen. 
Previously some GUI elements would layer over the menu at hand, this has now been fixed.
[*] Game starts before you do
A bug was present where on the start screen where you click 'Play', the game world would start without you. You would start getting hungry, animals could attack you etc until you click on play.
[*] Sync Creative Mode and InstaCraft
To activate these features, players would need to reconnect to their server in order for them to take effect. When you toggle them on the server, they should now sync and activate on the game in about 5 seconds.
[/list]

[h3]New Features[/h3]
[list]
[*] Auto Start Game
When you start the game from your desktop shortcut or through Steam, the server will now start minimized and the game will launch.
[*] Settings Menu: Unit System
If you are from the United States you might not be very familiar with Celsius or what Celsius is. That's Ok, you can now change the games unit system between Metric and Imperial. Imperial will show you Fahrenheit in stead of Celsius.
[*] We replaced the wells
Players will now in stead find a small body of water, typically found spawning randomly across the map, with a higher concentration in groves. These bodies can be collected from with the cup until they are depleted. When it rains, they will refill again. 
[/list]

[h3]Enhancements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Tweaking the rain
We tweaked the interval of rains so that you would have a head start in the first few minutes to get supplies and build a house before you would encounter cold and rain. 
Since Devlog 12 along with the rain we introduced wetness as a factor that exacerbates how cold the player is. If you were running around outside with no prospects of a shelter or a camp fire, by the time the first rain came around you would die from cold, which was brought on from wetness from being outside in the rain. We now scaled down the temperature fluctuations associated with the rain, as well as improved the players ability to withstand very hot or cold temperatures.
[*] Performance enhancement with the terrain
The current map in the game is 2 square kilometers or 1.25 square miles. We implemented a few changes so that foliage and the like around a player won't need so much rendering power without compromising quality. This will use about 100 MB of RAM though, but provides much smoother gameplay, especially on lower end computers. 
[*] New Animation for player
We fixed the players hatchet swing animation. The player will now correctly hold his tools and swing them properly. New animations to follow will be crouch walk, pick axe swing among others.
[*] Minor changes to the wolf
The wolf now identifies enemies differently. You can get up to about 10 meters to him and he will leave you alone, getting any closer and he will hear you. You can avoid this by crouch walking all the way up to him. If you get in his line of sight, crouched or not, he will spot you. He also won't pursue you very long anymore. He will also now sit once in a while when he's relaxing.
[/list]

This is it for now ladies and gentleman. We post on a Thursday so you can explore and enjoy all weekend. Rest assured we'll be neck deep enhancing, fixing, debugging, drawing, mixing audio, brain waving and drinking plenty of coffee in that time. Let's see what comes next time in Devlog 14.

Until then, 

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 12: A cold, wet and lonely day
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

For Devlog 12 we focused on making the wolf more efficient and worked on his placement to give him a better chance against the player. We also completed work on the first part of bringing temperature to Era of Survival. We also fixed a few other bugs as well. Let's dive in:

[h3]Temperature[/h3]
As of this build, players will now notice a new popup on the right side, above the belt, indicating your body temperature. There are many ways to influence this. When it rains and you're caught outside in the open, your player will get visibly wet. If you are wet, you will get much colder, especially if you stay outside in the rain. The raining itself will make you cold too. When you get too cold, you will die. On the other side, if you get too hot, you will burn - and get dehydrated quicker.

[h3]New sound[/h3]
Previously when you used any medicinal supplies, your avatar would make an 'Ouch' sound. He will now sound more satisfied :)

[h3]Fences[/h3]
We have retired our old fence and now offer one that suits your home more. This fence also comes with a gate. 

[h3]Health Recovery[/h3]
Players will notice that you now auto heal, like healing through the immune system. Over a period of time your health will systematically increase on its own. 

[h3]Another reach distance bug[/h3]
This time if you were too close to an object, like getting ready to chop down a tree, you would need to stand away a little bit to hit it. This has been fixed. You must now again stand up close to the object and still collect from it.

[h3]Press Q for Quick-Heal[/h3]
When you press Q on your keyboard, you will automatically use the medicinal supply closest to the start of your backpack. If you have 1 bandage in slot 2,  3 medkits in slot 8 and 2 bandages in slot 12, then when you press Q for the first time, 1 bandage would be used. If you pressed Q again, 1 medkit would be used. Arrange them for priority in your backpack. This is in line with making the wolf more potent.

[h3]Cost of Meds[/h3]
We have reviewed and changed the cost of supplies to craft medicinal supplies. This is in line with making the wolf more potent.

[h3]Modifications to the wolf[/h3]
The wolf will now attack you differently as well as be found in a different place. Yes, groves are nice.. Plenty food, water and essential supplies for players to thrive on. But as of this build, in order to indulge in the muchness that is our groves, you will have to first deal with the pack of wolves living in it.  

They will stick around their home grove, strolling around - until they notice you. They will chase you quite far beyond the grove and once they give up, they will walk back to their home. 

If you decide to take your chance and fight in stead, you should know that the wolf has changed slightly. Previously the wolf will run up to you and if he's in a certain range from you, and he hasn't bit you in the last few seconds, then he'll bite. Rinse and Repeat. Now, instead he will run up to you, turn to you and then bite, regardless of the time. He will have to get his mouth to you to get a bite. Meaning you can run around his left, or perhaps jump over him and get your shots in if you have to take him on with melee combat (Woops, the arrows aren't sharp enough yet..) 

We hope that our players welcome these changes and features. Whilst the topic count isn't much, we are confident that these changes make critical differences to shape Era into what our players want. We continue to invest our efforts to improve and expand Era of Survival, and to deliver on this promise to those who have chosen to support us already.

2 days late, but I hope you guys enjoy! :)

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 11: New sounds, server enhancements, bug fixes and rain
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

With this update we bring you the first element of our plan to incorporate weather and temperature into Era of Survival. We also added new sounds that makes gameplay more fun, we made adjustments to our server to speed things up and we got a few reported bugs out as well. Sadly we are not ready yet with body armor. Let's have a look:

[h2]Notable changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] [h2]New In-Game Settings menu[/h2]
We cleaned up the settings menu a little. From here it's much easier to add more settings for players to change.
We also fixed a bug where if you had the backpack and camp fire open, then the settings page would show and the camp fire dialog will be over it..
[*] [h2]New Sounds[/h2]
We added a few new sounds to make the game more engaging:
Tree fall over and crash sound
Wolf death sound
Sound of rain at different intensities
Sound of wind blowing
[*] [h2]Fixed stairs placement issue[/h2]
Some players could not place stairs properly on foundations, which prevented them from building multi-storey houses. You can now place your stairs on the foundation - as of this update, you can now rotate the stairs too
[*] [h2]You could open a storage box from 10 metres away[/h2]
Very handy, but not within arms length.. So we adjusted this to a more proper distance
[*] [h2]Rare count issue when drag and drop and combining items between the backpack and the storage box[/h2]
Here you would drag and drop wood together and if it's more than 200 (Maximum Stack Size) then you will get 200 + (insert wrong amount here). Remember that if you combine items in the inventory, if you add up above the 200 limit per slot, the difference will be added in a new slot, chosen from the first open or same slot by looking from the first one
[*] [h2]Change in speed for the dams[/h2]
Our dams were moving a little fast, more like streams down a river. Now they move more like a dam
[*] [h2]Change in Notifications[/h2]
When your inventory is full or your tool breaks, you will get a notification now.
[*] [h2]Camp Fires cook inconsistently[/h2]
We noticed that when players leave food in the fire, sometimes you would check after being away for a while, and even though the fire was on the whole time, it did not use any wood and did not cook any food. You can now safely trust your fire and leave it unattended to cook without supervision
[*] [h2]Avatar holding tools[/h2]
We noticed that the avatar was not holding certain tools properly. This has been corrected, but we intend on returning to this.
[*] [h2]Startup tips pop up every time the game starts[/h2]
We put these tips in at startup to help new players find their bearings in a matter of minutes. This was successful and indeed helpful. But after a while they become more intrusive than helpful. So now they will only show up in the first 10 starts, then it will stop showing up. When we send a game update, they will reset and start showing again for 10 times.
[*] [h2]We made it rain[/h2]
The grass is that green for a reason. This particular piece of land you now call home, has a very good rain fall around this time of year. Every couple of minutes the weather will change and (across the server) it will rain outside. Soon enough you will get cold if you stay outside and you would hide from the rain inside your warm house.
[/list]

That's it for now. We hope these changes and additions will help our players enjoy the best of Era of Survival. We stay committed to our project and those who have supported us - to continue expanding and improving our game. 

Until next time,

Cheers
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 10: New sounds, expanded drag and drop and new main menu
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

This week we prioritized improving the gameplay experience with new sounds, bug fixes and a couple more changes to bring the package together. 

[h3]Notable changes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] New main menu
We have changed our main menu, doing away with the still image and burning camp fire. Now you can get a good idea from what the game entails just by looking at the background on the main menu. We used the opportunity to demonstrate the build system and put a few animals on display.
[*] Door Frame to the wooden doorway.
To complete the look of our doorways, we gave the doorway a border. 
[*] GUI Drag and Drop support
We introduced limited drag and drop in the previous build to start getting feedback on how it's working. You could drag and drop supplies in your backpack only. In this build, you can now drag and drop supplies to your belt, storage boxes and the camp fire. You can still quick move supplies by right clicking them.
[*] Bug: Wolves won't chase you if you stand on a foundation.
This error occurred because the wolf would consider the foundation an obstacle. This has now been fixed so that walls etc is regarded as obstacles and not the foundation itself.
[*] Bug: Stone axe can't break the small storage box
This was an issue with identifying both objects on collision and has been fixed.
[*] Bug: Foundations can only be damaged by hitting it from the side.
This issue occurred because the top of the foundation was written to accommodate placement of objects on it. What this also caused is for the top of the foundation to be labeled differently, hence when referring to the amount of damage to apply on collision, it was nil - hence no damage. This has been fixed to still allow object placement, but to take damage regardless of where you hit it 
[*] Bug: Cannot place another wall after removing the previous one
Previously when you broke down a wall, the place holder to put the next one would not be available. Leaving a hole in your house. This also occurred with door placement. Both has been fixed.
[*] New Sounds: 
New stone hit sound
New sounds for the chicken
New sounds for storage boxes
[*] Smoothed jump animation
Players will notice that your character will still jump with his arms in the air, however he will now bring them down properly when landing. When jumping up a hill, he also won't keep his hands in the air anymore. He will also now smoothly transition between animations.
[/list]

We take the moment to congratulate ourselves on our 10th regular update for Era of Survival. We also want to congratulate our community, without which this achievement would've been a pipe dream. We strive to continue working with our community in moving Era of Survival forward. 

Until the next build :)

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 09: Enhancements and bug fixes
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

For this week we worked to improve current systems all over the game as well as fix a few bugs along the way. We also looked at making some tasks in the game a little simpler, like drag and drop in the inventory, easier object placement and tweaks to tool durability and tool efficiencies. 

[h3]Notables:[/h3]
[list]
[*] New features for your backpack
You can now drag and drop your supplies around to any slot you want. You can also drop similar supplies together to combine them together. Remember that your backpack has only 15 slots available. A small storage box has 10, and a large storage box has 20.
[*] Bug: Spinach not growing at the farm
When you planted spinach at the farm base, your progress would increase and your plot will still dry, but nothing would grow, in fact the plant type was nothing too. This is now fixed. Enjoy juicy spinach :)
[*] Enhancements to the object placement system
Players will notice a few differences when they put objects down now. When you hold something you can place down, like a camp fire, your character will now get out of the way so you can have a full view and put the object down. The object's placeholder will also now be where your red dot marker is aiming. Wall lights will also now face you when you put them down. They are no longer bound to only always inside lights.
[*] Tips on the loading screen
While you wait for the game to load when you log in to the server, you will now see handy tips that will help you survive better. Once the game is done loading, a button will appear that reads 'Play'. Click it to continue.
[*] New sound at the dams
Dams are a little more pleasant now, you can hear moving water and a few birds. Perfect for a sunset-by-the-dam house
[*] Internal tools upgrade
We mention this one to help assure our supporters that we are only interested in bringing something better to the table. Players that have used all of the available tools in game thus far, might have noticed that in very rare circumstances, some tools didn't react when used on some objects. Seeing that we have an ever growing amount of new objects, as well as a few more new tools on the roadmap, and a very primitive (Excel) way of keeping track of how objects and tools react, we had to take a minute and brainstorm on a better solution, then develop it. Now we are better equipped, and can deploy new objects and tools in game much faster, leaving more time (and brainpower) to drill hard and solve bitchy bugs.
[*] Bug: NPC characters passing through structures and rocks
NPCs like wolves would sometimes pursue you through any obstacle, except a high hill.. Through the rocks, through walls.. This has been fixed.
[*] When opening your menu, your character would keep breathing and breathing heavily. He will now stop to match the fact that he is standing still

[/list]

There are also minor bug fixes that we fixed whilst making all these changes. While we spend a fair amount of time on testing (versus development, marketing etc), we still prepare ourselves for new reported bugs. Sometimes you fix one thing, and it breaks something small elsewhere down the line of a completely different system. Next week is our 10th update to the game, and we want this to be a clear sign to our supporters that we remain dedicated. Even during the corona virus pandemic, our team members still work permanent jobs, but still make the time available to bring something better to the table. We remain committed to our cause, and have a long roadmap still to follow. 

Cheers for now,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 07: Bug Fixes
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

For this week we looked at fixing a few common bugs and made improvements as well, but we mainly focused to complete upgrading Era's files to Unity 2019. This will be a less noticeable update, but rest assured that foundations were laid in the process of upgrading. Without further ado:

[h3]Gap exploits around houses [/h3]
To the dismay of some player on the online server, others have figured out that (with great precision) you can actually reach a fireplace inside the house if it was placed very close to the wall on the inside, even though you are on the outside. This has been fixed

[h3]Harvesting from a dead body[/h3]
Similarly to above, when you harvest human meat from a dead body, if you hit at a weird angle, you can get an infinite supply of human meat

[h3]In game chat flickering[/h3]
In game chat update timers caused a quick disappear and then reappear act which was really annoying and distracting, no matter how infrequent it happens. Its fixed.

[h3]Server optimisation[/h3]
Our server provides data in layers to the game while you play, one of these layers (that dictates further away objects) wasn't working, which made a tree from far away stay standing when a player chops it down, and then the tree will finally disappear when you get close enough, which quite frankly, with the fog, gave it a sort of fog of war effect, but got fixed.

[h3]Black screen on start bug[/h3]
Sometimes when logging into the game, you would get stuck on the "Loading" screen forever - relogging in fixes it, but what happened is that there was data loss when transmitting the creation of your player on the server. We suspect this was due to packet loss, because the feedback we got showed that this was also happening with the creation of tools and weapons. Just very intermittently and when playing offline, very very rarely. But we've isolated where this happens and put measures in place to recover when there was an issue.

[h3]Avatar only runs, cant walk anymore[/h3]
Some players reported that their player can't walk, just idle or run. This was an interesting side effect that we might consider as something you can toggle in future, but we reverted back to walking for now.
Some players also told us that their avatars just kept running or walking when the menu got opened, even though the avatar was standing at the same place. Also been fixed.

[h3]Water well placement and sound[/h3]
Waterwells will now no longer just spawn randomly. Instead they are now confined to groves, where they could even come in pairs or more. This is one step closer out the door for the water wells though. We are looking into alternatives that can offer the same to the player, but would appear naturally in the environment. We also fixed the sound

[h3]Cup durability[/h3]
Lastly, your cup will now be able to serve you for much longer. Even though the cup was relatively cheap to make, it was still a hassle to wait 30 seconds for it to craft. So now it has increased durability.

We want to say thank you to our community without whom nothing would have been possible. We say thank you for your support. We also welcome our newcomers and as a developer, I implore current players to teach each other to play first, before just slicing and dicing one another.

As a team we stay committed to move forward with Era of Survival and with our roadmap, we hope to bring many new elements for the community to enjoy together.

Until next time,

Cheers!
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 06: Official Online Server
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,

This week we looked at getting an official server online, we worked on some damage indicators, we fixed a couple of bugs, we made trees fall over - but equally as important, we brainstormed on what comes after. 

Players will notice that this build is running quite smoother. We've started a process of upgrading our project with the aim of upgrading to the latest version of Unity. Because we started development back in 2017, Era was being developed with Unity version 2017. To get some specific bugs fixed, we need to migrate our scripts to a new language and then upgrade to Unity 2019, allowing us to finally get rid of some bugs that still exist since our launch back in February. 


[h2]Notable changes:[/h2]
[h3]Official online server[/h3]
You can now play on our first official server, located in California, USA. You can do so by going to "Play" in the main menu, then click on "Official Online Server". Note that a higher ping will have a negative effect on your gameplay. We recommend a ping around 150ms. You can still play offline by clicking on the "Play Offline" button found directly underneath the "Official Online Server" button
[h3]Walls cracking to indicate their health[/h3]
When you damage a wall now, you will see small cracks form to show its breaking, when the cracks are fully formed, the wall will disappear.
[h3]Trees fall over when chopped up[/h3]
When chopping down a tree and its depleted, it will now fall over and eventually disappear
[h3]Tool efficiency review[/h3]
We relooked tool efficiency across the board, tools are now stronger versus construction parts and construction parts are slightly weaker. 
[h3]Fixed bouncing camera near walls[/h3]
Previously when you would move around in your house and you got close to the wall on your right or close to the wall to your back, the camera would move to avoid clipping through the wall, weve now made changes so the camera smoothly avoids clipping through, in stead of just bouncing to the correct position


Era is getting in better shape come every build, and we've spend some time this week brainstorming on how Era will stand out and shine in its own spotlight. As the creators, we have a picture in mind of what we aim to make, guided by our players. We say thank you for the support from our community without which nothing would've been possible.

Until next week!

Cheers,
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 05: New items, cosmetics and playability
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

This week we looked at icons and models, as well as the flow of game play. We also got some more stubborn bugs out as detailed below.
Have a look at the first few minutes of game play [previewyoutube=yc5TXuEaHAI;leftthumb][/previewyoutube].
We are a small team of 1 programmer and 1 artist, but despite this we are making good progress to complete this phase of development. 

Whilst our list of fixes might still be long, we remain dedicated to our community and our customers to keep improving our product. Luckily we have a good system in place to guide us by effectively managing tasks across various game development departments.
[h2]Notable Bug fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Storage box does not sync last slot in its inventory to the server
[*] Server and multiplayer optimization - Syncing in game has been reduced, leading to smoother game play
[*] Issue with doorway blocking off contact with other items in the room when you didn't have a door
[*] Animals spawning on the same position - some users reported that all wolves will spawn at the exact same spot and have difficulty navigating on top of each other. This has now been fixed.
[*] Fixed placeholders that didn't light up green or red when trying to place them - at all, or just partially
[*] Spawn bug fix - You can now only spawn from your bed if you have died already, previously logging out and back in gave you the option to spawn by your bed, creating a teleport like hack for players
[/list]
[h2]Notable new items:[/h2]
[list]
[*] New terrain decor: Tropical plant
[*] New stone pickup rock. We replaced the small black rock with a new one
[*] A small storage box. This one costs less, but stores less things too
[*] Bandage - Heals less, but costs less. Perfect if you don't have plenty supplies but are in a bind
[/list]
[h2]Notable changes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] New item icons - Construction parts have new icons, including the wooden door and wooden stairs
[*] Cost decrease for stone pickaxe - This will help players collect wood faster, which will lead to them reaching stone age quicker and building bigger mansions and bases
[*] Collecting wolf meat - When you kill a wolf now, he will fall down on the ground in stead of disappearing. To get the meat, you must pick up the wolf body and clean it up in your inventory
[*] New wooden construction parts models - New wooden walls, wooden windows and wooden doorways, together completely changing the look and feel of your wooden palace!
[*] Door to doorway snapping color indicator - Like with placing foundations or walls, when you equip a door, you will see a place highlight where you should snap the door by the doorway.
[*] Moved Creative mode and InstaCraft to the server - The server admin should control this. The cheat 'advanced' has been disabled.
[*] You can now set the amount of wolves and chickens you want in game on the server - By default the server will keep 15 wolves in game and 20 chickens.
[/list]

We want to thank our players and our community of supporters for their help with submitting bugs and staying in touch with us as well as your patience. We might not get to responding to everybody, but as the game grows, we will start delegating work to new comers to the team to free us up more and ultimately allow us to focus more on game elements in depth. This is all nice and good, but none of this is possible without our supporters. And for that, we say Thank You! ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Devlog 04: Bugs, sounds and graphics
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

For this week we wanted to focus on the look, feel and sound of the game. This we got to after taking a sweep through and fixed bugs that got reported recently. 

[h2]Notables:[/h2]
[list]
[*] We finished programming and animating the chicken.
You can now hunt them, kill them, clean them, cook them and eat them. 
[*] We worked on the wolfs too. 
There were reports that wolves could stand stuck on a hill and couldn't come down or even chase the player, but would bite when the player got close. This has been fixed. 
[*] We polished up our rocks and worked on lighting. 
Shadows and lighting now better represent time of day. The color of water also now blends in better with the time of day.
[*] A new dam
Whilst this one is only the second one so far, it is now out there! Dams are infinite sources of drinkable water. Whilst water wells will deplete, dams wont. So if your aiming to start farming or want to choose a place to live, then stay close by the dam
[*] Improvements to the build system. 
We made some changes to indicative colors to make the process of building a base more simplistic. On occasions we noticed that foundations were peeking out through walls at the top also, this has also been fixed. You can also now build a ceiling two floors high, in stead of feeling cramped with a 1 floor level ceiling
[*] We made a serious improvement to client-server communication and latency. 
For best results whilst playing online, we recommend a ping of 150 or less 
[*] Your belt can now also occupy more items per slot
So in stead of having 1 wall in every slot and building them one by one, now you can have 200 walls in one slot and use the other slots for other construction parts to build your house faster. Together with creative mode and Instacraft, you can build up a massive site in minutes!
[/list]

[h2]Next on our to do[/h2]

This is what we have open at the moment that carries priority, whilst all might not make it to the final build come next Sunday, this should give you a good indication.[h3] 
Upcoming items and features [/h3]
[list]
[*] New sounds
We will add new sounds for collisions, like pickaxe hit stone kinda sounds. 
[*] Torch on wall
[*] Damage indicator for construction parts
[*] Server log in queue and player limit for server
[*] New wooden construction parts
[*] New stone construction parts
[*] A sword
[*] Rooftops
[*] In the name of transparency, we will start work on a demo version, so prospective players have the option to try the game before buying. This will help our customers make an informed decision on whether the game in its current state is value for their money or not, based on their own personal experience with the game
[*] New Animations
While this may not be ready come next week, we are currently busy making changes to the animations in the game. Whilst some are fine, some really needs to be updated.
[*] Set your own amount of wolves and chickens. If you want to take on 100 wolves, then we wont stop you, but in our experience, its a balance between quantity and quality. So if your PC's got the sauce, then we want you to be able to crank it up!
[/list]

Thanks for taking the time to read - and play our game.

Until next time :)
Jean

notes.title: Devlog 03: New trees and foliage
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

For this week, we worked on new trees, we added new bushes, different stones, different decor for the map as well as optimized the farming system and models some more. We also addressed reported bugs and want to thank everyone for their input. We're still short of a chicken and hit marks, but they will come too :)

[h1]Fixes and improvements[/h1]
[list]
[*] Tree and terrain decor LOD
This is for performance. Objects that are further away will now render in a lower quality to enhance performance, however this technique makes it difficult for the player to even notice the change in quality as further away objects would normally be too small to see the quality of anyway.
[*] Steam player name
When connecting to a server in the main menu, you will now notice that you cannot use a name of your own preference, in stead, your Steam name will now be used, it will also show in in-game chats as well as float above your head when close to other players
[*] Improvements with our new veggies
Our veggies have different life stages and different life stages to us means more models and more processing. We've spent the week optimizing all these models one by one to reduce their tax on the CPU and GPU, especially seeing that some servers have laid out farms in 15x15 plots
[*] Axe damage bug
A bug was found in the previous build where if you have 2 axes in your inventory and sent the last one to the belt, the first one in your inventory will go to the belt with the last ones reference, causing both axes to take damage when just the one is used. This has now been fixed.
[*] Bug report form bug
A cosmetic issue, but has been rectified. Some users reported that their caption texts would go red when they entered text in the bug report form. The form would still submit fine.
[*] Construction items hit sound
When you hit a wooden wall, it will now sound like it. 
[/list]

Theres minor bug fixes across the environment, we also have the nice water back without the lag tax

[h1]New additions[/h1]
[list]
[*] New Stone Rock
Players will no longer find our vertically upright stone to mine from, in stead we are introducing a new model that blends in better with the environment
[*] Logging back in
To avoid relogging into the server over and over and scoring wood every time, players will now just be whoever they were before they logged out with their inventory restored, back where they were. If you died while you were offline, you will respawn randomly or you can spawn by your bed
[*] Footsteps
We added footsteps for walking on wood. Next we'll put in footsteps for when the player goes through water, as soon as we create more water holes
[*] And of course, the new trees, bushes etc
We've added a new set of trees, bushes, stones, logs and textures with flowers and more dressings on the cards. Our finishing touch will be a wall that surrounds the map, effectively isolating the player inside
[/list]

[h1]Next week[/h1]
We have plans and work according to a structured task system, so we have a good idea of whats coming next week, but making empty promises is just not cool, so we try to avoid making too many promises, rather under promise and over deliver, so heres a short list :)
[list]
[*] Combination cooking
We want players to start cooking with all these meats and new veggies. So we will introduce combo cooking, where you add different produce with a meat and get a very filling stew that provides health regeneration and a hunger kick.
[*] Corn seeds and carrots 
If you want to plant corn and wheat, then lets do it! Mielie pap, anyone?
[*] Name your bed
It can get confusing to identify your bed when you have 4 and they have 4 digit numbers for names, lets change it! 
[/list]

Until next time ~ Happy surviving!
Jean

notes.title: Quick update - performance and more
notes.content:
Hello everyone :),

Due to the nature of the game, we understand that regular (perhaps too regular) updates can really ruin things for players playing online for a few hours when the server needs to be updated (and your map wiped), however we had to finish work on performance issues that weren't yet ready with yesterdays update.
