notes.title: Devlog 01: Bashing bugs and making barriers
notes.content:
Hello everyone :),

Its been quite an eventful 7 days since our launch. With very mixed reviews, through discussions, reviews and private chats with players, we have spent a proportional amount of time processing and changing our game towards completion of this phase. As we've said before, we intended the launch build to have the basics up and running, cooking, resource collection, building and multiplayer. Whilst these features are still basic, they have enough power currently to pull off an afternoon of multiplayer gameplay. This we can obviously see from internal alpha testers.

With this said, we've noticed that some elements weren't working for others and have made changes to rectify this. Some were very noticeable and bothering, so we prioritized our available time to fix them first.

[h1]Notable bug fixes:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Network communications improvement. In a client server environment, there is always room for improvement, especially when the server communicates over the internet
[*] Resource balancing on the server
[*] Improved picking up items, you can now pick up things like mushrooms and fibres from further away, except when you have a tool or weapon in your hand.
[*] Improved snapping in the build system and made it generally feel easier to work with
[*] Thirst was too potent, you now won't get thirsty so quick
[*] Speedup loading time between main menu and the game
[*] Placement didn't work when players tried to place items, but weren't looking at the place holder at the time
[*] Removed glasspane
[*] Removed basic shelter
[*] Durability and damage on tools have been reviewed and edited. Tools will yield slightly different results
[*] For the moment we have added a barrier close to the edges of the map to prevent players from falling off, this will be replaced with unexplorable mountains later on
[*] Foods have been resized to be spotted easier. Has anybody found the Turnips?
[*] Pickaxe no longer cost stone
[/list]

We've fixed various other minor bugs that was also reported. We want to remind players that you can submit bug reports in game from the setting menu as well.

[h1]Notable new features:[/h1]
[list]
[*] New dam where you can fetch water
[*] Changed the wooden block and stone block. You'll now find a stack of wood to pick up. The same goes for the stone block
[*] Map has been changed, rocks have been moved and more terrain decor has been added. The walk through stones have been removed.
[/list]


[h1]Notable differences to the server:[/h1]
[list]
[*] We've changed the look of the server so players can launch a 32bit or 64bit version of the game. When you start the game in Steam, the launcher/server will run, from here you can launch the game from the top right corner. 
[/list]

[h1]Next week:[/h1]

Come next weeks Devlog, we will be introducing 7 new foods that will be available in the game. Some of them you will be able to replant where you want, and this way you will be able to start your own farm! With this we will also introduce a chicken, which you will be able to get food from. You will also be able to have your thirst replenished when eating certain foods. Other foods will eventually be used in combination cooking, where you can add carrots, meat and onions to make a stew by the fire. This will be more filling and help the player heal too.

We are closing off spam jumping up rocks, but the initial idea was for players to strategically use them to get away from hostile animals and people, so we are between disabling going up the stones completely, or just preventing spam jumping up where theres not enough support underneath your character.

We will by then also be ready with object hit marks. When you hit a tree with an axe, it should leave a mark! 

We are currently setting up an official online server for players to play on. At the same time we will be implementing a new server selection screen on the main menu, so you can browse registered online servers or play offline on your own. We are also busy removing the "Player Name" from the main menu, this will be replaced with your Steam account name.

We will also move the "Save" button in the Settings menu to next to "Draw Distance" as this button updates the draw distance. It does not save the games state or progress.

We have also added Creative mode and Instacraft. They can be accessed by using the cheat "advanced", although this cheat will eventually be moved to the server so the server admin can toggle this on and off.



Whilst Era of Survival is still in development, we maintain that our product offers value to customers in its current state. It just takes more than running around in a circle to play. The environment and its resources are what players must use to out play other players and build better and stronger bases. The point of the game is to become the best player, by collecting resources and fighting off anything that prevents you from becoming the strongest player, in an economical sense, and soon a physical sense.

Thanks for reading!
Jean
